# Effect parameters

Every parameter each effect reads, taken from the renderer itself.

Read this before writing an effect node. Effects look their parameters up **by
name**, and a name that does not match is not an error — the effect uses its
default and carries on. A misspelled or invented parameter validates, renders,
and silently does nothing, so the names here are the whole contract.

Order does not matter. (The one exception is `custom-sksl`, which has no fixed
names: its uniforms bind positionally, flattened in the order the `parameters`
array declares them — `number` and `boolean` take one float, `point` two,
`color` four. That order *is* the ABI.)

`number` and `point` parameters also require `minimum` and `maximum` fields on
the node, which are metadata for editors; the ranges below are what the
renderer actually clamps to.

## `blur`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Clamped to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | number | 8 | 0 or more |
| `sigmaX` | number | — | 0 or more |
| `sigmaY` | number | — | 0 or more |

## `color-matrix`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Clamped to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `m0` … `m19` | number | identity matrix | — |

Row-major, 20 entries. Defaults are the identity matrix, so an
unset entry leaves the channel untouched. The alpha row is `m15`…`m19`.

| `contrast` | number | 1 | 0 … 4 |

## `custom-sksl`

Names are yours. The uniforms in your shader bind positionally against the
flattened `parameters` array, so the declaration order in the shader and the
order of that array have to agree. `number` and `boolean` take one float,
`point` two, `color` four.

What the engine gives you, and what it does not:

- **One child shader, `inputImage`** — the node named by `inputId`, already
  drawn. There is no backdrop child; a custom shader cannot refract what is
  behind it, only transform its own input. That is what `glass` is for.
- **No implicit uniforms.** The built-in shaders get `time`, `origin` and
  `deviceScale` appended for free; yours gets exactly the parameters you
  declared and nothing else. If you want time, keyframe a `number` parameter —
  a phase running 0 to 2π across the composition also makes the loop close.
- **`main`'s coordinate is in device pixels**, origin at the top left of the
  effect's pass. Not composition units, not normalised.
- **`eval()` returns premultiplied colour.** Unpremultiply before touching
  `rgb`, or the maths is wrong wherever alpha is not 1. `unpremul()` is
  available and uses Skia's own epsilon.
- **`point` parameters are converted to device pixels for you**, so they share
  a space with `main`'s coordinate and comparing them is correct at any render
  scale.
- **The pass covers the whole canvas by default.** A custom shader is not
  bounded to its input the way `glass` is, because the engine cannot know how
  far your shader reaches. Three number parameters narrow it —
  `boundsPadding`, or `boundsPaddingX` and `boundsPaddingY` — read **by
  name**, giving the margin around the input's bounds that your effect needs.
  Note what that costs: they are ordinary parameters, so each one also occupies
  a positional float in your uniform array and your shader has to declare a
  matching uniform. Bounding the pass is a real saving on a large canvas; it is
  not free.
- **`number` parameters are passed through unchanged**, because the engine
  cannot tell a distance from a count or an angle. A number meaning "pixels"
  therefore stays in *composition* units while your coordinate is in device
  pixels, and a shader mixing the two is correct at exactly one size — which is
  how an effect drifts off its own artwork in a preview.

  **Ask for the scale.** Declare two more floats than your parameters supply,
  conventionally `uniform float2 renderScale;` **last**, and the engine appends
  the device scale. Divide by it to work in composition units:

  ```glsl
  float d = length(p - centre) / renderScale.x;   // composition units
  ```

  Opt-in rather than always appended, because uniforms bind positionally and
  appending unconditionally would change the ABI of every shader already
  written.
